in  Criminal Appeal No.332 of 2017 Suraj Shreshth ..... Appellant/applicant  Vs.
State of Uttarakhand .....
Mr. Sandeep Adhikari, learned legal-aid counsel for  the appellant/applicant, appeared through video  conferencing.

Mr. K.S. Bohra, learned D.A.G. along with Mr. S.C.
 Dumka, learned A.G.A. for the State of Uttarakhand.

Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J. (Oral)
Heard learned counsel for the parties.
2. Learned counsel for the appellant/applicant has pressed this bail application for his release on bail.

3. The appellant/applicant is under incarceration on his conviction vide judgment and order dated 17.10.2017 passed by learned Fast Track Court/Special Judge (POCSO)/Additional Sessions Judge,
Dehradu in Special Sessions Trial No.12 of 2015, State Vs. Suraj Shreshth, for the offence punishable under Sections 506 IPC and Section 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (POCSO), 2012 and was mainly sentenced for 07 years' R.I. with fine of Rs.30,000/- under Section 4 of POCSO Act, in respect of victim No.1 and under Sections 376(2)(i), 506 IPC and Section 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (POCSO), 2012 and was mainly sentenced for 10 years' R.I. with fine of Rs.30,000/- under Section 376(2)(i) IPC, in respect of victim No.2.
4.

sentences.text: It is contended by learned counsel for the appellant that the appellant/applicant is falsely implicated in the aforesaid crime and he is wrongly convicted.

He also contended that the appellant/
applicant is in custody from the date of his arrest i.e.21.11.2014, therefore, he has spent more than 9 years under incarceration.
He stated that the appellant/applicant deserves to be released on bail on that sole basis.

5. Per contra, learned State Counsel submits that the appellant/applicant was convicted for committing sexual assault on two victims, one of whom was minor of about 14 years' of age at the Suraj Shreshth .....

He further submits that the victims have throughout supported the case of prosecution, therefore, the appellant/applicant cannot be released on bail.

6. Having considered the rival submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties and having gone through the statements of victims and medical examination report of both the victims; this Court is of the view, that the appellant/applicant-Suraj Shreshth does not deserve to be released on bail at this stage.
Accordingly, bail application deserves to be rejected.

8. List this criminal appeal for final hearing on 21.08.2024.
(Pankaj Purohit, J.) 14.06.2024 PN/-
